maria_k: Heads-up — onboarding run for rdx-7b-quant4 shows weird token misalignment after ~1.1k tokens. Not a crash, but outputs start repeating earlier context.
cheng_l: hmm, repeating where exactly? example?
maria_k: pasted minimal repro below. use long prompt with anchored system message + multi-paragraph user text. After ~1100 tokens the model repeats the first paragraph verbatim.
devon_h: could be a KV index wrap or RoPE scaling mismatch when we compress to int4. Did you try the fp16 baseline?
maria_k: yes baseline fp16 is clean up to 8k. quant4 only reproduces. int8 reduces fidelity but no repetition.
sam_r: can you share the run command + model artifact id?
maria_k: ```
./bin/infer --model rdx-7b-quant4:v2026.03 --prompt-file tests/long_anchor.txt --max-tokens 4096 --kv-enabled --emit-kv-debug
```
ops-bot: deploy note — this run used dedicated staging-gpu-3, image rdx/infer:canary-2026-03-18
cheng_l: thanks. the `--emit-kv-debug` logs are key. Any anomalies in key idx numbers or timestamps?
maria_k: extracted a tiny snippet from kv debug around the flip:
```
KV IDX: 1107 -> embedding_slot 1107
KV WRITE: shard0 pos=1107 rot-phase=0.9982
KV READ: shard0 pos=1107 rot-phase=0.6611  <-- mismatch
```
cheng_l: that read rot-phase delta looks huge. suggests encoding/sinusoid scaling differs between prefill and decode paths.
devon_h: do we use different rotary scaling for prefill vs autoreg? there was a fast-path we added for quantized kernels that approximates scale.
sam_r: I remember PR #4123 added a packed-rotary path for int4 to speed prefill; could be leaking alternative state.
maria_k: repro script attached in the run logs runs two passes: (1) prefill full prompt, dump KV; (2) decode on same KV. If we re-run decode using the fp16 runtime against the quantized KV, it reads fine.
cheng_l: that means the KV layout itself is okay; the decoder path in quantized runtime is interpreting the rot-phase differently.
devon_h: hypothesis: scale factor applied per-token was quantized to 8-bit and we overflow the fixed-point accumulator at token ~1100 when phase values wrap, producing aliasing.
sam_r: can we try a quick patch to the quantized rotary mul to use a conservative float path for phase values > 0.9? i.e. fall back to float for high-phase magnitude.
cheng_l: quick hack I ran locally: in kernels/rotary_quant.cu
```
if (abs(rot_phase) > 0.9f) {
  out = float_mul(input, rot_sin, rot_cos);
} else {
  out = quant_fast_rot(input, rot_sin_q, rot_cos_q);
}
```
Ran full longprompt test: repetition disappeared for that case.
maria_k: nice! any perf hit?
cheng_l: measurable but small: ~2.5% p99 latency increase for the path when triggered, overall negligible since trigger frequency is low.
devon_h: we should add a regression test in nightly with an anchor-heavy prompt to catch this.
sam_r: agree. also add a telemetry flag when fallback is taken so we can aggregate frequency across customers.
ops-bot: epic:created-ticket #ML-824 anchor-phase-quant-fallback (assignee: cheng_l)
maria_k: next steps I propose:
- add unit + e2e test (long prompt, quant4) in ml-regressions
- enable telemetry counter `rotary_quant_fallback.v1`
- patch release for canary and run A/B against staging
- follow-up: investigate whether different quantization rounding reduces need for fallback
cheng_l: I'll open a PR with tests + telemetry. also will bisect the packed-rotary PR to see minimal diff.
devon_h: two follow-ups: add a small doc in eng-ml/notes about interplay of RoPE magnitude, token index and fixed-point rounding; and consider a model-agnostic flag `--ropex-compat` for customers
sam_r: FYI I ran benchmark on throughput: fallback triggered <0.4% of tokens on our corpus, so cost is minimal.
maria_k: thanks everyone. I'll run a longer soak on staging after PR lands and report back here. :thumbsup:
cheng_l: thanks — loop me in when PR is ready for review.
